$comment: ★★ A `.s` THAT ENDS INSIDE AN UNTERMINATED `/*` ASSEMBLES AND RUNS, WITH gas's WARNING (P68 round 8, D-ASM-UNTERMINATED-BLOCK-COMMENT-AT-END-OF-FILE-REFUSED). ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23: GNU as 2.42 assembles such a file (the comment opened on the SAME line as the final `ret`, no newline at the end), warning 'end of file in comment', and the program returns 42; clang 18.1.3 refuses it ('unterminated comment'). The references split on ACCEPTANCE, so the union accepts; the WARNING is gas's, and it is kept because a missing `*/` silently swallowing the rest of a file must not be silent. DSS refused it with `P_UnterminatedComment`. The dialect's `block-comment` mode now declares `atEndOfInput: closesWithWarning`: the comment closes at the end of the input with `P_ClosedByEndOfInput` at its OPENER, and only then does the implied end-of-input newline (`endOfInputImplies`) terminate the `ret` line, which is the order gas uses. The swallowed lines are load-bearing: a comment closed anywhere earlier would expose a second `main:`. ★ RED-ON-DISABLE: set `atEndOfInput` back to its default and the example is refused again; drop `endOfInputImplies` and the `ret` line has no terminator. The `release` arm pins only that naming the release pipeline does not break the assembly path.

expectWarnings.$comment: the `/*` opener on the `ret` line; the comment runs to the end of the input
